subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw accept the bounded longer isolated-cron setup watchdog proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219, or require a different configurable policy before fixing this issue?
rationale: The fix shape changes default cron availability behavior for stuck setup, and AGENTS.md/VISION.md set a high bar for new config surfaces, so automation should not choose the product policy alone.

options.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
options.body: Merge the PR-style policy that keeps a 60s floor, derives from the job timeout, and caps setup at 10 minutes without adding a new config key.

options.title: Require operator config
options.body: Ask for a narrow config surface and docs/schema coverage if maintainers want deployments to tune setup watchdogs explicitly.

options.title: Keep 60s and split diagnostics
options.body: Reject longer setup occupancy and pursue only phase diagnostics or backend-specific repairs for the distinct stall classes.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
recommendation.body: Merge the PR-style policy that keeps a 60s floor, derives from the job timeout, and caps setup at 10 minutes without adding a new config key.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses cron runtime policy and config-surface guidance, and this owner has recent history in the cron timer boundary plus broader repository direction.
